scores.M_value: USAspending confirms Switchblade is a real, large, recently-obligated production line ($406.5M FY20-22 base contract is the company's #1 DoD award). J-Book corpus does not contain Switchblade as a named PE because our 410-PE corpus is focused on RDT&E/Procurement line items extracted for other cohorts (DARPA / SDA / AF RDT&E / quantum etc.) and does not cover Army Other Procurement line items for sUAS/TMS. The Ukraine RQ-20B Puma award filed 2023 ($323M) shows a major forward demand pull through Ukraine FMS that AVAV does not even describe in the FY22 10-K -- this is upside relative to the disclosed narrative, not downside.
scores.interpretation: PASS. Heuristic 7 applies: NOT_FOUND in J-Book is not a red flag because the J-Book corpus is hand-curated for the defense-tech cohort and does not yet include Switchblade / Raven / Puma procurement lines (these live in Army Other Procurement and Army OPA P-40 exhibits that the corpus does not index). The orthogonal usaspending verifier confirms the Switchblade claim is materially TRUE -- it's the company's largest single DoD award. Calibration heuristic 7: treat NOT_FOUND as UNVERIFIABLE unless the company names a PE explicitly; AVAV does not name a PE. The independent positive evidence from usaspending (1) Switchblade is real, (2) >$400M obligated, (3) Ukraine pull is increasing demand, all support the claim. Coverage gap flagged.

scores.M_value: Telerob generated $29.2M revenue but a $12.1M operating LOSS in FY22 -- a -42% operating margin in its first full year under AVAV ownership. USAspending shows zero direct DoD prime contracts for Telerob, meaning the 'expand into DoD EOD/CBRN' narrative had not yet materialized in obligations by the cutoff. The acquisition is technologically adjacent (robotics) but the operating-loss disclosure is itself a soft red flag on rollup execution.
scores.interpretation: MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY. The acquisition coherence signal is not strongly negative on its face (robotics adjacency is real), but the disclosed $12.1M loss on $29.2M revenue plus zero USAspending direct DoD obligations indicates the integration is at minimum behind schedule. Per the rollup-thesis lens, FY22 Telerob is dilutive while the company narrates it as accretive growth. Materiality is moderate since Telerob is small relative to total revenue.

calibration_notes.cohort_pattern_applicability: LOW. The J-Book Exposure Divergence pattern is designed to flag companies that name specific Pentagon PEs (e.g., 'AFRL Quantum Networking', 'SDA Tracking Layer T3') in narrative, where the J-Book then shows those PEs going unfunded. AVAV's FY22 10-K does NOT name specific PEs or specific named DoD programs-of-record in that style. AVAV's pattern is product-line-and-customer disclosure (Switchblade / Puma / Raven sold to Army / SOCOM under Family of Systems IDIQs). The framework's primary verifier (pentagon_jbook) returns NOT_FOUND across the board not because programs are unfunded, but because the 410-PE corpus does not cover Army Other Procurement / Army OPA P-40 sUAS/TMS line items.
calibration_notes.coverage_gap: J-Book corpus does not currently index: (a) Army Other Procurement Switchblade / LMAMS line item, (b) Army Other Procurement Raven/Puma/sUAS Family of Systems line item, (c) Army RDT&E FTUAS / Future Tactical UAS PE, (d) Army Short Range Reconnaissance PE. To make this cohort productive against sUAS/TMS primes, these P-40 line items should be added to programs.json.
calibration_notes.j_book_fires_on_jbook_grounded_claims: 0 of 5 J-Book-grounded claims (C1, C2, C3, C4, C5). All returned NOT_FOUND or spurious matches -- none returned an actionable FUNDED/UNFUNDED status.
calibration_notes.orthogonal_verifier_signal: usaspending was the load-bearing verifier on this filing. Net signal: AVAV's disclosed Switchblade / Puma / Raven / Arcturus narratives are corroborated as REAL by obligations. Telerob is the one weakness (zero direct DoD obligations + 42% operating loss in first full year).
